name: The Fortress Gates
subtitle: The first assault on the seat of darkness

shard.name: Seal Fragment of the Void
shard.description: A shard of pure absence — not dark, not cold, simply without. Holding it feels like standing at the edge of something that does not end.

scenes.narration: The fortress materializes before them like a wound in the sky — black stone that seems to swallow light, towers that twist in ways that hurt to look at. It is not built. It is grown. Fed. Alive.
Aya stands at the front, the four Seal Fragments held in her hands. They pulse with light — answering each other, drawing closer to completion.

dialogue.speaker: Aya
dialogue.text: Four pieces broken and reclaimed. One fragment remains — inside that darkness. And one more answer: why.

dialogue.speaker: Tao
dialogue.text: I have guided the dead across the veil for so long. I can feel the weight of souls trapped in that place. Screaming.

dialogue.speaker: Rei
dialogue.text: Then we give them peace. We give them freedom. We tear down this monument to fear.

dialogue.speaker: Lulu
dialogue.text: Six of us. One darkness. The math is simple.

chapters.title: The Void Citadel
chapters.map_hint: Push through the Void Citadel — the Void Warden guards the fortress gate beyond.

pre_dialogue.speaker: narrator
pre_dialogue.text: The Void Citadel stretches before them — black stone that swallows light, towers that twist in ways that hurt to look at. Shadow-creatures pour from every passage, guardians of the outer ring.

pre_dialogue.speaker: Rei
pre_dialogue.text: Let them come. We break through.

pre_dialogue.speaker: Ria
pre_dialogue.text: The eidolons sense the echoes. This place was not always dark. Once, it held light. They can feel what used to sing in its halls.

pre_dialogue.speaker: Valka
pre_dialogue.text: Then we reclaim it. Not for ourselves — for what was stolen from it.

post_dialogue.speaker: narrator
post_dialogue.text: At the heart of the citadel, a figure coalesces from shadow — ancient, vast, wearing robes of starlight corrupted to ash. The Void Warden.

post_dialogue.speaker: narrator
post_dialogue.text: Void Warden: Valdris is pleased you reached this far. He did not think you would.

post_dialogue.speaker: Aya
post_dialogue.text: Then he has learned nothing about us.

scenes.narration: Inside the outer walls, the fortress is different to what they expected. Not a weapon. Not a dungeon. A palace, once — its bones still visible beneath the corruption. Arched corridors that were meant to carry light. Libraries with empty shelves where knowledge used to live. Someone built this place to be beautiful.

dialogue.speaker: Tao
dialogue.text: This was not a fortress. It was a home.

dialogue.speaker: Ria
dialogue.text: The eidolons sense the tragedy here. A place that was meant to be beautiful, now corrupted into a weapon.

dialogue.speaker: Rei
dialogue.text: The Oracle's records say he built this. Before the hunger. When he was still someone who built things.

scenes.narration: At the centre of the first courtyard, suspended in shadow like a wound held open, something vast and winged turns slowly. The Consumed Angel — what was once a scholar's companion, the last created thing Valdris loved before love became impossible for him. Its face is gone. But its wings still remember the shape of flight.

dialogue.speaker: Valka
dialogue.text: Once, a being of light. Something he made — or found — or loved. Before. I can see what it was through the corruption. It was meant to be a guardian. A protector.

dialogue.speaker: Tao
dialogue.text: ...Yes. Even the things he loved. They were not safe from what he became.

dialogue.speaker: Lulu
dialogue.text: Then we free it. Whatever is left inside — we free it.

pre_dialogue.speaker: narrator
pre_dialogue.text: The Consumed Angel descends. Not attacking — not yet. It circles them once, as if remembering a shape it used to protect. Then the corruption overwhelms the memory, and it becomes a weapon.

pre_dialogue.speaker: Aya
pre_dialogue.text: It is not choosing this. That matters. It also does not change what we have to do.

pre_dialogue.speaker: Rei
pre_dialogue.text: Purpose consumed. Will erased. This is what Valdris does to everything he touches — it forgets itself. We remind it what it was.

pre_dialogue.speaker: Valka
pre_dialogue.text: If there is anything left of what it chose to be, this will free it. Hold nothing back.

pre_dialogue.speaker: Lulu
pre_dialogue.text: It was meant to protect. We will end what is trapping it here. That is the most we can give it.

pre_dialogue.speaker: Tao
pre_dialogue.text: For the scholar who made it. For whoever it was before. And for everything he took from himself by consuming it.

post_dialogue.speaker: narrator
post_dialogue.text: The Consumed Angel dissolves — not with violence, but with the slow release of something that has been held past the point of endurance. Its wings scatter into light. For one breath, the courtyard is bright.

post_dialogue.speaker: Lulu
post_dialogue.text: ...There it is. That was what it was supposed to be.

post_dialogue.speaker: Aya
post_dialogue.text: The outer ring is broken. The fortress is weakening at its core. We have the Fragment. We do not stop.

post_dialogue.speaker: Rei
post_dialogue.text: He will feel this. He built that thing, and now it is gone. Even if he cannot feel grief, he will feel the gap where it was. Good.

post_dialogue.speaker: Drake
post_dialogue.text: The inner sanctum. The Shadow Titan. Whatever is left of the man inside that darkness — we face it now. Together.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The communication stone pulses. For the first time since they entered the Citadel, Essabella's voice cuts through the static.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Essabella: The guardian you just unmade. The Consumed Angel. That was Commander Veleth. The first to join me when I fell.

dialogue.speaker: Rei
dialogue.text: Those were your soldiers in the outer ring. He didn't just kill them. He kept them.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Essabella: Yes. They were my soldiers.

dialogue.speaker: Lulu
dialogue.text: We freed them, Essabella. I am so sorry.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Essabella: I made calculations that were wrong. I thought she had more time. That is my weight to carry. You must carry yourselves to the inner sanctum. Do not let her ending be for nothing.
